description: Unidentified Hunter F.56A on concrete pylons just outside the Hasimara AFS entrance gate, painted overall in the blue Thunderbolts aerobatic scheme (No.20 Sqn), no serial visible, cockpit stripped, plaque gives only a type history. Visible from outside the gate. Source warbirds.in (photos Rahul Devnath, 2009).

MD.450 Ouragan displayed on a platform in front of the Officers Mess at Hasimara, IAF grey with No.47 Sqn Black Archers motif on nose, canopy replaced by sheet metal, nose wheel reversed. Dedicated 3 April 1986 by ACM D A La Fontaine as No.47 Sqn memorial (unit history book). Source warbirds.in (photos Rahul Devnath), bharat-rakshak database (preserved Hasimara).

Late-production HAL Gnat E1046 upgraded to Ajeet standard (plaque says Ajeet), mounted on a metal frame at 40 degrees nose-up in front of a major building/hangar at Hasimara, markings of No.22 Sqn Swifts. Mosmap fix 26.702531 89.368399. Source warbirds.in (photos Sanjay Simha, Rahul Devnath), bharat-rakshak (preserved Hasimara AFS).

MiG-27M TS600 preserved next to the cricket/PT ground south-west of the Hasimara runway (26.688579 89.343160 per commenter Amartya Ghose, March 2024). A second unidentified MiG-27M is displayed north of the runway/hangars. Source warbirds.in Feb 2024 post and comments; bharat-rakshak lists TS-600 at Hasimara cricket ground.
Second of two MiG-27Ms displayed at Hasimara, this one on the northern side of the runway and hangars; identity not yet established. Source warbirds.in (Feb/Mar 2024).
